question: Ajay invested some money in HDFC at 4% per annum rate of interest. What would be the corresponding simple interest (in ₹) if after 2 years, Ajay got ₹204 as compound interest, considering annual compounding?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For 2 years, the direct relationship between Compound Interest (CI) and Simple Interest (SI) is given by the formula:

CI ÷ SI = (200 + R) ÷ 200

204 ÷ SI = (200 + 4) ÷ 200

204 ÷ SI = 204 ÷ 200

SI = 200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rate (R) = 4% per annum

Time (T) = 2 years

Compound Interest (CI) = ₹204

**Formula Used:**

CI = P[(1 + R ÷ 100)² − 1]

SI = (P × R × T) ÷
